Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

Whom do I call first when I am afraid?

In prayer you say 'You alone we ask for help.' Whom did you call first when afraid? The answer is yours.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

It is You we worship and You we ask for help.

Quran · Al-Fatihah 1:5

Translation

You shall fear Yahweh your God; and you shall serve him, and shall swear by his name.

Original · Hebrew

אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ תִּירָ֖א וְאֹת֣וֹ תַעֲבֹ֑ד וּבִשְׁמ֖וֹ תִּשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 6:13

World English Bible

You have said this sentence many thousands of times. In the Arabic the word You stands first, twice, and that is how the language says “You alone”. A sentence repeated so often can turn into a sound. So here is a plain test, and you are its only witness: what was true of you on the day you needed it? Nothing here will check your answer. All that is asked is that you look.

A question for you

Go back to the last time you were truly frightened. What was the first name on your lips? Write it if you like, or only remember it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ ۖ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ كَفُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when adversity touches you at sea, lost are [all] those you invoke except for Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away [from Him]. And ever is man ungrateful.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:67

Translation

Then they cry to Yahweh in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress. He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Then they are glad because it is calm, so he brings them to their desired haven.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּֽ֝מִמְּצֽוּקֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹצִיאֵֽם׃ יָקֵ֣ם סְ֭עָרָה לִדְמָמָ֑ה וַ֝יֶּחֱשׁ֗וּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם׃ וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כִֽי־יִשְׁתֹּ֑קוּ וַ֝יַּנְחֵ֗ם אֶל־מְח֥וֹז חֶפְצָֽם׃

the Psalms · 107:28-30

World English Bible

The verse reports something about people. When harm comes at sea, everyone you used to call on drops out of mind, and One remains. It describes what is left when every means has failed, the ship included. There is a limit to keep in view. Calling a mother, a friend or an ambulance is asking people for what people can give, and the Quran records that too (28:15). The verse is about the moment after that, when no person can reach you.

A question for you

When you look back at that moment, which of these is closest?

If you sayOne call was left, and it went to God.
ThenThen you have lived what the verse describes. The question it leaves is what became of that call once you were back on land.
If you sayI called on someone I love who is close to God.
ThenLove reaches for those who have comforted us, and that love is worth honouring. Keep it, and carry one question to the next part: in their own worst hour, whom did they call?
If you sayI called someone near me who could help.
ThenAsking a person for what a person can give is ordinary, and the Quran records it. The verse's moment comes after that, when no one can reach you.
If you sayI froze, or felt nothing.
ThenThat is an honest answer, and the verse does not argue with it. Many people have no words in that moment. Nothing here depends on your having felt otherwise.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّى مُمِدُّكُم بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Remember] when you were asking help of your Lord, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand from the angels, following one another."

Quran · Al-Anfal 8:9

Translation

God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַנַּעַר֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ אֶל־הָגָר֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ מַה־לָּ֣ךְ הָגָ֑ר אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא־שָֽׁם׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 21:17

World English Bible

Now look at the people you already love. At Badr the believers were few and afraid, and the Prophet was among them. The verse records what they did in that hour: they cried out to their Lord for rescue, and He answered. None of them stood above that cry. Whatever name rose to your lips, this is what those you follow did with their fear.

A question for you

If the person you love most in faith were beside you in that moment, what would they tell you to do?

The same in the other books

Translation

Only fear Yahweh, and serve him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things he has done for you.

Original · Hebrew

אַ֣ךְ ׀ יְר֣אוּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֛וֹ בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י רְא֔וּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הִגְדִּ֖ל עִמָּכֶֽם׃

1 Samuel · 12:24

World English Bible

Translation

Serve Yahweh with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

Original · Hebrew

עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה בְּיִרְאָ֑ה וְ֝גִ֗ילוּ בִּרְעָדָֽה׃

the Psalms · 2:11

World English Bible

Give thyself more diligently to reflection: know thyself: take counsel with the Godhead: without God put thine hand unto nothing!

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 115

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

Translation

Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in you. My soul, you have said to Yahweh, “You are my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing.”

Original · Hebrew

מִכְתָּ֥ם לְדָוִ֑ד שָֽׁמְרֵ֥נִי אֵ֝֗ל כִּֽי־חָסִ֥יתִי בָֽךְ׃ אָמַ֣רְתְּ לַֽ֭יהוָה אֲדֹנָ֣י אָ֑תָּה ט֝וֹבָתִ֗י בַּל־עָלֶֽיךָ׃

the Psalms · 16:1-2

World English Bible

Your reflection

Once you were safe, what did you do with your fear?
